Path of the Animal Spirit.about: Your rage calls up the spirit of a beast that fights beside you. The hunters of the Emberwood and the high moors tell stories about the spirit that walks with them.
features: When you enter your Rage, a spectral beast appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet. Choose its look: Bear, Stag or Hound. It can't be hurt or targeted, and it lasts until your Rage ends. On your turn you can move it up to your Speed (no action needed). The first attack you make on each of your turns against a creature within 5 feet of the beast has Advantage.
You always know the direction of the nearest beast within 1 mile, and you have Advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks.
While your Rage lasts, once per turn when you hit a creature within 5 feet of your spirit beast, the beast bites it for extra damage equal to your Rage Damage bonus.
While raging, as a Bonus Action you can swap places with your spirit beast. You don't provoke Opportunity Attacks when you do.
Once per Long Rest, when you drop to 0 Hit Points while your spirit beast is present, you drop to 1 Hit Point instead and the beast vanishes.

Path of the Kinwarden.about: You fight for the ones you've sworn to protect, and the dead of your family stand behind you. The old clans say a kinwarden never fights alone.
features: When you enter your Rage, name up to a number of allies equal to your Proficiency Bonus. They are your kin until the Rage ends.
While raging, when a kin you can see within 5 feet is hit by an attack, you can use your Reaction to become the target instead. You take the damage with your Rage resistance applying.

Kin within 30 feet of you have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition. When a kin drops to 0 Hit Points, you can use your Reaction to move up to your Speed toward them and gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Barbarian level.
Once per Long Rest, you can cast Speak with Dead without spending mana. The dead answer up to three questions and can't lie to you.
When a creature hits you or a kin, you can mark it until the end of your next turn. You have Advantage on attack rolls against the marked creature, and it can't take the Disengage action.

Path of the Stormcaller.about: The storm lives in your chest, and every blow you take feeds it. Stormcallers walk into the weather and come out holding the lightning.
features: While raging, each time you take damage from an attack, you gain 1 Charge, to a maximum of 5. Your Charges end when your Rage ends.
When you hit with a melee attack while raging, you can spend all of your Charges. The hit deals an extra 1d6 Lightning damage per Charge spent.
While raging, you have Resistance to Lightning and Thunder damage. While you have 3 or more Charges, your Speed increases by 10 feet.

When you are hit by an attack while raging, you can use your Reaction and spend 2 Charges. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and your Constitution modifier) or take 2d8 Thunder damage and be pushed 10 feet away.

You start each Rage with 3 Charges, and Discharge uses d8s. Once per Long Rest, when you Discharge, creatures of your choice within 15 feet of you take Lightning damage equal to the Discharge damage (half on a successful Dexterity saving throw).

Path of the Fervent.about: Your rage is a sworn vow, spoken before the fight begins. Keep it and you are terrible. Break it and the fury leaves you.
features: When you enter your Rage, choose a Vow. If you break it, your Rage ends. Guard: choose a creature within 30 feet. While you are within 5 feet of it, you both gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. The Vow breaks if it drops to 0 Hit Points or you end your turn more than 30 feet from it. Avenge: choose a creature you can see. You have Advantage on your first attack each turn against it and deal extra damage equal to your Rage Damage bonus. The Vow ends when it is dead or out of sight. Endure: you don't move on your turn. In return you have Advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws, and at the start of each of your turns you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
You can swear two different Vows when you enter your Rage.
Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, up to a number of allies equal to your Proficiency Bonus within 30 feet share the benefits of your Vows until your Rage ends.
Once per Long Rest, when you break a Vow, your Rage doesn't end. Instead you take psychic damage equal to twice your Barbarian level, which can't be reduced.

Path of the Feral Shape.about: When the rage takes you, you stop being a person. Feral Shape barbarians wear the shape of the beast they've hunted all their lives.
features: When you enter your Rage, you can take the shape of a beast: Bear, Boar or Panther. You become Large if there is space. Your Unarmed Strikes deal 1d10 plus your Strength modifier and count as magical. Bear: you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Barbarian level. Boar: you can't be knocked Prone, and you can move through the space of Medium or smaller creatures. Panther: you gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and your jump distances are doubled.
While in your beast shape, you have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed, and Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on smell.

While in your beast shape, as a Bonus Action you can move up to 10 feet. The first creature you hit after moving at least 20 feet on a turn takes extra damage equal to your Rage Damage bonus and must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and your Strength modifier) or be knocked Prone.

While in your beast shape, your weapon and Unarmed Strike attacks score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20, and when you reduce a creature to 0 Hit Points you regain Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier.

Path of the Wildborn.about: You were raised where the world's magic runs raw, and your rage draws on it. A Wildborn never knows which surge will answer, so they choose before they need it.
features: When you finish a Long Rest, choose three Surges from the list below. When you enter your Rage, you can spend one of them. A spent Surge is gone until you finish a Long Rest. Flare: creatures of your choice within 10 feet must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and your Constitution modifier) or have the Blinded condition until the end of your next turn. Thorns: until your Rage ends, a creature that hits you with a melee attack takes 1d6 plus your Proficiency Bonus Piercing damage. Mend: you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Barbarian level plus your Constitution modifier. Gale: creatures of your choice within 15 feet must succeed on a Strength saving throw (same DC) or be pushed 10 feet away from you. Echo: the next weapon attack you hit with deals an extra die of weapon damage. Spark: until your Rage ends, your weapon attacks deal an extra 1d6 Lightning damage.
You know when a spell is cast within 60 feet of you, and what school it belongs to.
Your hand holds four Surges. When you finish a Short Rest, you can swap one Surge for another.
When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you regain one spent Surge.
You can spend two Surges at once when you enter your Rage, and you can also spend a Surge as a Bonus Action once during each Rage.

Path of the Titan.about: Your rage swells you until the doorway is too small. Titans of the old stories walked the isles before the elves, and you carry a little of that size.
features: At the start of each of your turns while raging, you gain a Growth stage, to a maximum of 3. Your stages reset when your Rage ends. Stage 1: your reach increases by 5 feet. Stage 2: you become Large if there is space, and you have Advantage on Strength checks and saving throws. Stage 3: once per turn, when you hit with a melee attack, you deal extra damage equal to your Rage Damage bonus.
Your carrying, pushing, dragging and lifting limits are doubled. You can hurl improvised objects with a range of 20/60 feet.

While at Stage 2 or higher, when you move at least 10 feet on your turn, creatures of your choice within 5 feet of your path must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and your Strength modifier) or have the Prone condition.

As a Bonus Action while raging, you can make an Athletics check contested by a Large or smaller creature you are grappling. On a success, you throw it up to 30 feet. It takes 3d8 Bludgeoning damage and lands Prone.
You begin each Rage at Stage 2. At Stage 3 you become Huge if there is space, and your reach is 10 feet greater than normal.

Battle Tactician.about: A tactician who fuels combat maneuvers with superiority dice, and who wins fights by thinking three moves ahead. Captains of the Dornish Army train their officers in these techniques before they lead a single charge.
features: Learn three maneuvers and gain four d8 superiority dice, back on a short rest. Spend a die to trip, disarm, push, feint, parry, rally an ally and more. More maneuvers at 7th, 10th and 15th.
Study a creature for a minute to learn how it compares to you in two traits (Strength, AC, HP, class levels and so on).
If you roll initiative with no superiority dice left, regain one.

Spellblade.about: A fighter who blends swordplay with abjuration and evocation magic. Knights who serve the great houses often take this path, learning enough magic to win a duel without giving up the sword.
features: Bond with up to two weapons: they can't be disarmed and you can summon one to your hand as a bonus action.

Your mana fuels a small wizard repertoire, mostly abjuration and evocation spells. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
When you cast a cantrip as an action, make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
A creature you hit has disadvantage on its next save against your spell before the end of your next turn.
When you Action Surge, teleport up to 30 ft.
When you cast a spell as an action, make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

Arcane Bowman.about: An archer who weaves magic into arrows, and who can bend a shot around a shield or drop a monster with a single fletched bolt. The archers of the Garrison are famous for it.
features: Learn Arcana or Nature, and Prestidigitation or Druidcraft.
Know two Arrow Art options (sunder, lure, burst, snare, pierce, hunt, shade, weaken) and use them twice per short rest when you hit with an arrow. More options at 7th, 10th, 15th and 18th.
When you miss with a magic arrow, use a bonus action to reroll the attack against a different target within 60 ft.
If you roll initiative with no Arrow Art uses left, regain one.

Rider Knight.about: A mounted warrior and bodyguard who locks enemies in place and keeps the people beside them safe. Rider Knights guard the roads into [[Loreaon]] and ride with the nobles who pay for their steel.
features: One skill (Animal Handling, History, Insight, Performance or Persuasion) or a language.
Advantage on saves against falling off your mount, land on your feet if you fall, and mount or dismount cheaply.
Mark creatures you hit: they have disadvantage attacking anyone else, and if they do you can make a bonus action attack with extra damage.
Reaction: add 1d8 to an ally's AC against an attack, and give them resistance if it still hits.
Creatures that move within your reach provoke opportunity attacks, and a hit stops them in place.
Moving 10 ft straight before a hit can knock the target prone.
An extra reaction each round, only for opportunity attacks.

Honor Blade.about: Unshakeable resolve turns into precise, relentless strikes, and the samurai’s honor is the first thing they protect. Their courtly manners hide a deadly edge that few enemies see coming.
features: One skill (History, Insight, Performance or Persuasion) or a language.
Bonus action, three times per long rest: advantage on attacks this turn and some temporary HP.
Add Wisdom to Persuasion and gain Wisdom save proficiency (or another save if you have it).
If you roll initiative with no Battle Spirit uses left, regain one.
Trade advantage on one attack for an extra attack.
When you drop to 0 HP, take an extra full turn before falling, once per long rest.

Mirrorguard.about: You fight alongside an echo of yourself from another possible timeline, one that can attack, swap places with you and take blows meant for you. Some in the isles say the echo is simply the knight’s better self.
features: Summon a translucent echo (AC 14 + proficiency, 1 HP). You can attack from its space, swap places with it, and it makes opportunity attacks.
When you take the Attack action, make one extra attack through your echo. Uses equal to Con modifier per long rest.
See and hear through your echo, and send it up to 1,000 ft away.
Your echo throws itself in front of an attack meant for an ally, once per short rest.
When your echo is destroyed, gain temporary HP a few times per long rest.
Two echoes at once, and regain an Unleash the Twin use when you roll initiative with none left.

Mindforged.about: Psionic power adds force to your blows and shields your allies from harm. Mindforged are rare in the isles, and most of them keep their talents to themselves.
features: Mind dice (d6, rising with level), back on a long rest; regain one per short rest. Spend one to add force damage to a hit, cut damage to an ally, or move a creature or object with your mind.
Psi-powered leap (fly for a turn) and Mind Thrust (push or knock prone with your force strikes).
Resistance to psychic damage; spend a die to end charm or fear on yourself.
Bonus action: give a few creatures half cover for a minute, once per long rest (or spend a die).
Cast Telekinesis without spending mana once per long rest (or spend a die), and attack as a bonus action while concentrating on it.

Runebound.about: Giant runes are carved into your gear, and you can grow huge when the fight calls for it. The smiths of [[Dragonsneck]] carve these runes for their best defenders.
features: Smith's tools and the Giant language.
Know two runes (sky, ember, rime, ore, crag, gale) with a passive gift and an activated power each, once per short rest. More runes at 7th, 10th and 15th.
Bonus action: become Large for a minute, with advantage on Strength checks and saves and an extra 1d6 damage once per turn. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
Reaction: force a creature to reroll an attack against an ally, a few times per long rest.
Grow a little taller permanently; Colossal Might damage rises to 1d8.
Use each rune's power twice per short rest.
Colossal Might makes you up to Huge, with 1d10 extra damage and more reach.

Way of Shade.about: A ninja-like monk who moves between shadows and strikes from places no one expects. Shadow monks in the cities are often hired for jobs that never reach the watch.
features: You train in the shadows and learn the arts of darkness and silence. Spend 2 ki to cast Darkness, Darkvision, Pass without Trace or Silence without spending mana; learn Minor Illusion.

You step out of the light and into the dark, appearing where the shadows fall. In dim light or darkness, teleport 60 ft to another dark spot as a bonus action and gain advantage on your next melee attack.
You disappear into the gloom and stay hidden until you choose to strike. Become invisible in dim light or darkness until you attack or cast.
You strike at the enemy as it falls to another's blow. Reaction: attack a creature within 5 ft that just got hit by someone else.

Way of the Four Winds.about: You channel ki into elemental disciplines, bending fire, water, earth and air to your will. Monks of the Four Elements are welcome in most temples, and most of them prefer the open road.
features: You learn to draw the elements through your ki and shape them into disciplines. Learn Element Sense and one discipline (more at 6th, 11th and 17th). Disciplines spend ki to produce effects like Fangs of the Ember Serpent, Tide Lash or Shape the Tide, some copying spells without spending mana.
Your disciplines grow with you, and each one gives you a new elemental power. Learn another discipline; you can swap one out when you gain a discipline.
Your disciplines grow stronger as you spend more ki on them. Learn another discipline and spend more ki to empower them.
Your mastery of the elements lets you learn one more discipline. Learn another discipline.

Way of the Last Breath.about: A monk who studies death and feeds on it, and who finds strength in the last breath of an enemy. Other monks keep their distance from them, and the Tomb Domain priests have their own opinions.
features: When you reduce a creature within 5 ft of you to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your monk level plus your Wisdom modifier.
As an action, a wave of dread sweeps out from you. Each creature within 30 ft must make a Wisdom save or become frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
Death's grip loosens for you. When you drop to 0 hit points, you can spend 1 ki point to drop to 1 hit point instead.
You can channel your ki into a killing touch. Spend 1 to 10 ki points, and a creature you touch takes 2d10 necrotic damage per ki point spent. It makes a Constitution save for half damage.

Way of the Sunlit Spirit.about: You hurl ki as searing radiant light, and your strikes burn with the brightness of the dawn. Monks of the Sun Soul are often sent to the front of a holy war, and they count the days until they can rest.
features: You channel the sun's light through your ki, and it burns out from your fists. A 30 ft ranged radiant attack that uses your martial arts die; can replace attacks and be used with Flurry.
You can hurl a bolt of radiant light at a distance. After the Attack action, spend 2 ki to cast Burning Hands as a bonus action (more ki for a stronger version).
Your light sears the air and burns those who stand near you. Action: a 20 ft radius burst of radiant light (Con save); spend ki to strengthen it.
Your body shines like the dawn, and foes who touch you get burned. Shed bright light, and creatures that hit you in melee take radiant damage.

Way of the Tipsy Fist.about: Lurching, staggering moves make you impossible to pin down, and your wine is never far from hand. The taverns of the port towns have a soft spot for these monks, and they always know who is buying the next round.
features: Years of tavern nights taught you a few things you can use in a fight. Performance and brewer's supplies.
Your staggering footwork makes you hard to pin down, and you keep moving as you strike. Flurry of Blows also gives you Disengage and +10 ft speed.
You sway and dodge in a way that makes an opponent's blow glance off. Stand up for 5 ft of movement, and redirect a missed melee attack to another creature.
Your luck is never wholly gone, and a little ki can turn a bad roll around. Spend 2 ki to cancel disadvantage on a check, attack or save.
In your frenzy you can strike at a crowd, each blow finding a different foe. Flurry of Blows can make up to five attacks if each hits a different target.

Way of the Swordmaster.about: A weapon master whose chosen weapons become part of their martial arts. A kensei treats a blade as a sacred bond, and few are ever parted from theirs.
features: You take up the weapons of the kensei and treat them as an extension of your body. Pick kensei weapons that count as monk weapons, gain an AC bonus when you skip an attack, and add extra damage to ranged hits as a bonus action.
Your chosen weapon hums with power and cuts through what ordinary steel cannot. Your kensei weapons count as magical; spend ki for extra damage on a hit.
You can focus your ki into your blade to strike harder for a short while. Spend up to 3 ki to give a kensei weapon that bonus to attack and damage for a minute.
Your blade finds its mark when it counts most. Reroll a missed monk-weapon attack once per turn.

Way of the Spiritbound.about: You summon your spirit self: first spectral arms, then a visage, and finally a full spirit body that fights beside you. Astral monks say their guide comes from another plane, though few have seen it.
features: You call forth your spirit self, a spirit that answers your will. Spend 1 ki to summon spectral arms that strike using Wisdom with longer reach, and push enemies away when they appear.
Your astral face shows you the hidden and speaks with a voice that commands attention. Your astral face lets you see in magical darkness and speak with intimidating or quiet clarity.
Your astral body is a shield as well as a weapon. With arms and visage out, deflect energy damage and add extra damage on a hit.
Your spirit self becomes a full spirit for a moment, and you fight as one. Spend 5 ki to manifest everything at once: AC bonus and an extra attack.

Way of Compassion.about: Healers and harbingers who carry both life and death in their hands. Mercy monks are the ones called to tend the wounded after a battle, and they are also the ones who end the suffering of the dying.
features: Insight and Medicine proficiency, and the herbalism kit.
Spend 1 ki to heal a creature with a martial arts die + Wisdom; can replace a Flurry strike.
Once per turn, spend 1 ki on a hit for extra necrotic damage.
Hand of Healing also cures a disease or condition; Hand of Harm can poison.
Replace each Flurry of Blows strike with Hand of Healing, and use Hand of Harm on one for free.
Spend 5 ki to bring back a creature that died in the last 24 hours, once per long rest.

Night Killer.about: A killer who strikes first and from hiding, and who can vanish after a job without a trace. The guilds of the big cities pay assassins well, and the watch pays them even more to stay quiet.
features: You study the art of the killing blow and learn how to disappear afterward. Disguise kit and poisoner's kit.
Your trade requires specialist tools for disguise and poison. Advantage against creatures that haven't acted yet in combat, and any hit on a surprised creature is a critical hit.
You strike before your target can react and leave nothing behind. Spend a week and some gold to build a solid false identity.
You are a master of the false face, and you can wear another life like a cloak. Copy someone's speech, writing and mannerisms after studying them for three hours.
A surprised target has no time to save itself, and your blow lands cleanly. Hitting a surprised creature forces a Con save or doubles the damage.

Arcane Rogue.about: A rogue with enchantment and illusion magic, who makes a crowd forget what it saw. Sleight-of-hand fixers are welcome in the courts and feared in the taverns, and they can be both on the same night.
features: Your mana fuels a small wizard repertoire, mostly enchantment and illusion. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability. Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Your Mage Hand is invisible and can pick locks, plant or lift objects at range.
If you're hidden when you cast, the target has disadvantage on its save.
Bonus action: your mage hand distracts a creature, giving you advantage on attacks against it.
Reaction when a spell targets you: force a save to negate it and steal the spell for 8 hours, once per long rest.

Seeker.about: A detective who reads lies and finds the weak point in every story. Seekers serve the watch, the courts and private clients who cannot trust the official answer.
features: Insight rolls to spot lies treat a die below 8 as an 8.
Bonus action: Perception to spot hidden things or Investigation to find clues.
Bonus action: Insight against a target's Deception to gain Sneak Attack on it without advantage for a minute.
Advantage on Perception and Investigation if you move half speed or less.
Sense illusions, shapechangers and magic deception nearby, a few times per long rest.
Sneak Attack deals an extra 3d6 against a target you've read with Insight.

Schemer.about: A schemer who directs allies from the shadows, and who turns other people’s strengths into their own. Schemers are rarely seen in the same room as the crime they planned.
features: You learn the arts of intrigue, and a few tools of the trade help you deceive. A gaming set, a disguise kit, two languages, and the knack of mimicking accents.
You can aid your allies from the edge of a fight. Help as a bonus action, from up to 30 ft away.
You read others and learn what makes them tick. Study a creature for a minute to learn how it compares to you in mental abilities and other traits.
You turn an attack aimed at you toward a creature that stands in your shadow. Reaction: redirect an attack aimed at you to a creature giving you cover.
Your mind is a fortress against prying eyes, and your lies are hard to see through. Your thoughts can't be read; you can feed false thoughts, and magic can't force the truth out of you.

Pathfinder.about: A skirmisher and wilderness expert who moves quickly, sees everything and strikes when the enemy least expects it. Pathfinders guard the borders of [[Doresmere]] and the roads between the great houses.
features: You move like a shadow through the wild, always ready to slip away. Reaction: move half your speed when an enemy ends its turn next to you, without provoking.
You are at home in the wild and know how to live off the land. Proficiency and expertise in Nature and Survival.
Your steps are quick and sure, and you cover ground faster than most. +10 ft speed (walk, climb, swim).
You are hard to spot in the first moments of battle, and you make the most of it. Advantage on initiative, and your first target in the first round is easier for everyone to hit.
You can strike again the moment your first blow lands. A bonus action attack after the Attack action, which can Sneak Attack a different target.

Duelist.about: A flashy duelist who darts in and out of combat with a grin and a flourish. Duelists are the favorites of the taverns and the tavern-keepers’ daughters, and they are rarely short of a wager.
features: A creature you attack in melee can't make opportunity attacks against you that turn.
Add Charisma to initiative, and Sneak Attack a lone enemy in a one-on-one without advantage.
Persuasion against Insight: an enemy fixates on you (disadvantage on others) or a non-hostile creature is charmed.
Bonus action: advantage on your next Acrobatics or Athletics check this turn.
Reroll a missed attack with advantage, once per short rest.

Deadwhisper.about: A rogue touched by death, who steals the knowledge and the last words of the dead. Deadwhispers are shunned by the church and tolerated by the Tomb Domain, and they do not much care who approves.
features: After a rest, gain proficiency in a skill or tool of your choice.
After Sneak Attack, deal half the Sneak Attack dice as necrotic to another creature nearby. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
Catch a soul trinket when someone dies nearby; use them for advantage on saves, extra wails, or to ask a spirit a question.
Become spectral for 10 minutes: fly slowly, pass through objects, attackers have disadvantage.
Wails of Dread hits both targets with necrotic, and you always find a token after a rest if you have none.

Thoughtblade.about: Psionic blades formed from your mind cut through armor and thought alike. Thoughtblades are rare, and the few in the isles tend to keep to themselves.
features: Mind dice (d6, rising with level); spend them to boost failed checks or speak telepathically.
Manifest blades of psychic energy to make melee or thrown attacks, with a bonus action second blade.
Spend a die to turn a miss into a hit, or teleport with a thrown blade.
Become invisible for an hour, once per long rest (or spend a die).
A Sneak Attack with your blades can stun the target (Wis save), once per long rest (or spend dice).

Lore Domain.about: Priests of learning who know secrets, read minds and keep the old records. Knowledge clerics serve Korinth and are often found in the libraries of [[Akorsrest]].
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Two extra languages, and proficiency with double bonus in two of Arcana, History, Nature or Religion.
Gain proficiency in any skill or tool for 10 minutes.
Read a creature's surface thoughts (Wis save), then cast Suggestion on it without spending mana.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
Meditate to see recent events around an object you hold or the area you're in.

Dawn Domain.about: Bearers of fire and dawn who burn away darkness and the things that hide in it. Light clerics are the first to be sent when the night gets dangerous.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack against you, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Dispel magical darkness and deal radiant damage to hostile creatures within 30 ft (Con save halves).
Warding Glare can protect allies too.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
Shed sunlight; enemies in it have disadvantage on saves against fire and radiant spells.

Wildwood Domain.about: Servants of the wild who charm beasts, shape plants and speak for the forests. Nature clerics are welcome in the villages and feared by the lumbermen.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Learn a druid cantrip and one of Animal Handling, Nature or Survival.
Channel Divinity: Charm of the Wild
Charm beasts and plant creatures within 30 ft for a minute (Wis save).
Reaction: give resistance to acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage to a creature within 30 ft.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra cold, fire or lightning damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Command charmed beasts and plants with a bonus action.

Thunder Domain.about: Storm priests who answer blows with thunder and lightning, and who see the sea as a holy thing. Thorum’s followers in the port towns speak of them with awe.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Reaction: a creature that hits you takes lightning or thunder damage (Dex save halves), Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Make a lightning or thunder spell deal maximum damage.
Your lightning damage can push Large or smaller creatures 10 ft.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra thunder damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Fly at your walking speed when outdoors and not underground.

Mischief Domain.about: Tricksters who deceive with illusions and doubles, and who serve the god of mischief when the rules get in the way. Trickery clerics are good company until they are not.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Give a creature advantage on Stealth for an hour.
Create an illusory duplicate you can cast through, and gain advantage when you and it flank a creature.
Become invisible until the end of your next turn.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra poison damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).

Battle Domain.about: Champions of battle who strike with divine force and who believe every fight is a test of faith. War clerics ride with the knightly orders and fight in the front lines of every holy war.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Make a weapon attack as a bonus action after the Attack action, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
+10 to an attack roll after you see the roll.
Reaction: give an ally +10 to an attack roll.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra damage of the weapon's type (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks.

Anvil Domain.about: Smith-priests who craft and wear the finest armor, and who believe the work of the hand is a prayer. Forge clerics are welcome in the great smithies of the isles.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
After a long rest, give a weapon or armor +1 until your next long rest.
An hour-long ritual to create a simple metal item worth up to 100 gp.
Resistance to fire, and +1 AC in heavy armor.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra fire damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Immunity to fire, and resistance to nonmagical weapon damage in heavy armor.

Tomb Domain.about: Guardians against undeath who keep the dying alive and finish the doomed with mercy. Grave clerics walk the cemeteries of the old cities and keep watch over the dead.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Healing a creature at 0 HP uses maximum dice; Spare the Dying works at 30 ft as a bonus action.
Sense undead within 60 ft, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Curse a creature so the next attack against it deals double damage.
Reaction: turn a critical hit on you or an ally into a normal hit, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
When an enemy dies nearby, you or an ally regains HP equal to its Hit Dice.

Law Domain.about: Enforcers of law who command allies and punish disobedience. Order clerics serve the church’s courts and the king’s peace, and they expect obedience from everyone.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Heavy armor, and Intimidation or Persuasion.
When you cast a spell with mana on an ally, they can make one attack as a reaction.
Charm creatures of your choice within 30 ft until your next turn and make them drop what they hold (Wis save).
Cast enchantment spells as a bonus action, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra psychic damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Mark a creature you hit; the next ally hit on it adds psychic damage.

Harmony Domain.about: Peacemakers who bind allies together and calm the rage of a crowd. Peace clerics are often sent to settle disputes between the great houses.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Bond a few creatures: once per turn each can add a d4 to an attack, check or save while near another bonded creature.
Move without provoking and heal each creature you pass.
Bonded creatures can teleport to each other to take damage for one another.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
The bond reaches 60 ft, and the creature that takes the hit gains resistance.

Dusk Domain.about: Guardians of the in-between hours, who shield travellers from the dark and the things that walk in it. Twilight clerics keep the night watches at the gates of the isles.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Darkvision 300 ft, which you can share.
Give a creature advantage on its next initiative roll.
A sphere of dim light around you for a minute: each turn allies in it gain temporary HP or shake off charm or fear.
Fly in dim light or darkness for a minute, a few times per long rest.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra radiant damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Your sanctuary also gives half cover.

Sigil Domain.about: Scholars of magic who study the workings of the arcane and the divine together. Arcana clerics are sought out by mages who want a god’s blessing on their spells.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Arcana proficiency and two wizard cantrips.
Turn (and later banish) celestials, elementals, fey and fiends.
When you heal an ally with a spell, also end one spell on them.
Add Wisdom to cleric cantrip damage.
Add wizard spells of 6th to 9th level to your list (you still need the charges or channel to cast them).

Grim Domain.about: Priests of the end of life who see death as a guide, not an enemy. Death clerics of Azrul keep the Bone Hall beneath [[Akorsrest]] and answer questions from the dead.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your domain's spells suit your god; learn them from tomes or your temple at the usual cost.
Learn a necromancy cantrip that can target two creatures next to each other.
Melee hit deals extra necrotic damage: 5 + twice your cleric level.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals extra necrotic damage (1d8, 2d8 at 14th).
Single-target necromancy spells of 1st to 5th level can target a second creature.

Oath of the Elders.about: You keep the old oaths to the forests, the rivers and the gods of the land, and you protect the living world from those who would burn it. Druids and paladins of the Ancients speak to each other as old friends.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Spectral vines restrain a creature (Str or Dex save).
Turn fey and fiends, revealing their true forms.
You and allies within 10 ft have resistance to spell damage (30 ft at 18th).
Drop to 1 HP instead of 0 once per long rest, and you stop aging.
Transform for a minute, once per long rest: regain HP each turn, cast faster, and enemies nearby have disadvantage on saves against you.

Oath of Reckoning.about: You swear to hunt down those who have done great wrong, and you do not stop until the debt is paid. Vengeful paladins are welcome in the courts of justice and feared in the taverns of the guilty.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Frighten one creature and freeze its speed (Wis save).
Advantage on attacks against one creature for a minute.
After an opportunity attack hit, move half your speed without provoking.
Reaction: attack the target of your Hate's Mark when it attacks.
Grow wings and a menacing aura for an hour, once per long rest.

Oathbroken.about: A paladin who has broken their oath and now serves a darker cause. Oathbroken are hunted by their old orders, and they have their own reasons for everything they do.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Take control of an undead creature (Wis save).
You and undead or fiends within 10 ft add Charisma to melee damage (30 ft at 18th).
Resistance to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing and slashing.
A minute-long aura of gloom that frightens and damages enemies, once per long rest.

Oath of Dominion.about: You swear to bring the enemy to heel and rule the lands you take. Conquest paladins are the iron fist of the great houses, and they remember every castle they ever took.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Frightened enemies within 10 ft can't move and take psychic damage (30 ft at 18th).
Creatures that hit you take psychic damage equal to your Charisma.
A minute of resistance to all damage, an extra attack and critical hits on 19–20, once per long rest.

Oath of Mercy.about: You swear to end fights without bloodshed where you can, and to give a second chance to those who have fallen. Redemption paladins are often sent to talk with rebels and bandits before the swords come out.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Reaction: a creature that hurts another takes radiant damage equal to what it dealt (Wis save halves).
Reaction: take the damage meant for an ally within 10 ft (30 ft at 18th).
Regain HP at the end of your turn while below half.
Resistance to all damage, and attackers take radiant damage back, unless you attack them.

Oath of Renown.about: You swear to live and die by deeds worth singing about. Glory paladins are the heroes of the taverns, and they are rarely careful about the cost of a good song.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Advantage on Athletics and Acrobatics, and bigger jumps and carrying, for 10 minutes.
After Divine Smite, share temporary HP among allies.
+10 ft speed, and allies who start near you move faster (aura grows at 18th).
Reaction: add Charisma to AC against an attack and strike back if it misses.
For a minute, once per long rest: advantage on Charisma checks, turn a miss into a hit once per turn, and reroll failed saves.

Oath of the Nightwatch.about: You swear to guard the people against the unnatural and the things that come out of the dark. Nightwatch keep the night patrols at the walls of [[Loreaon]] and at the lonely watchtowers beyond.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. Your oath's spells suit your vows; learn them from tomes or your order at the usual cost.
Allies gain advantage on Int, Wis and Cha saves for a minute.
Turn aberrations, celestials, elementals, fey and fiends.
You and allies add your proficiency bonus to initiative (aura grows at 18th).
Reaction: when an ally succeeds on a mental save, deal force damage to the creature that forced it.
For a minute, once per long rest: truesight, advantage on attacks against extraplanar creatures, and banish them on a hit.

The Fey Court.about: Your patron is a powerful creature of the fey, who gives you gifts and asks for favors in return. Fey bargains are binding, and an archfey’s price is always higher than it first seems.
features: Your patron's fey nature gives you spells tied to its court. Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
You can enchant the minds of foes and send them fleeing. Charm or frighten creatures in a 10 ft cube (Wis save), once per short rest.
When you are struck, you slip into a veil of mist and vanish. When you take damage, turn invisible and teleport 60 ft, once per short rest.
You turn your patron's gift into a shield against the charms of others. Immune to charm, and turn charm attempts back on the caster.
You trap a foe inside an illusion of its own making. Trap a creature in an illusory realm for a minute, once per short rest.

The Outer Horror.about: Your patron is an alien mind from beyond the stars, and its knowledge fills your head like a flood. Few mortals survive long enough to learn what it truly wants.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Speak telepathically to any creature within 30 ft.
Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack; if it misses, gain advantage on your next attack against that creature. Once per short rest.
Your thoughts can't be read, resistance to psychic damage, and psychic attackers get hurt back.
Touch an incapacitated humanoid to charm it permanently and talk to it telepathically.

The Radiant Patron.about: Your patron is a being of light, and its favors pour through you like sunshine. Celestial pact-holders are welcome in the churches, though the Akorian bishops watch them closely.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
A pool of d6s (1 + warlock level) to heal creatures at range with a bonus action. Back on a long rest.
Resistance to radiant damage; add Charisma to one fire or radiant spell damage roll.
Gain temporary HP after each rest, and give some to allies.
When you'd make a death save, spring back to half HP and blind nearby enemies with radiant light, once per long rest.

The Bladebound.about: Your patron is a blade of ancient power, and the steel you carry answers to your will. Bladebounds are sought out by the knightly orders and avoided by everyone who has seen one fight.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Curse a creature: extra damage equal to your proficiency, crits on 19–20, and heal when it dies. Once per short rest.
Medium armor, shields and martial weapons; use Charisma for attacks with a chosen weapon.
Raise a slain humanoid as a specter that serves you until your next long rest.
Attacks from your cursed target miss half the time (roll a d6, 4+ misses).
When your cursed target dies, move the curse to another creature.

The Deep Patron.about: Your patron is a creature of the deep sea, and its tentacles and currents answer your call. Fathomless warlocks are most often found in the port towns of the coast, and the sailors are not sure whether to thank them or pray against them.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Summon a spectral tentacle that lashes for cold damage and slows, as a bonus action. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
Resistance to cold, and talk to anything underwater.
Your tentacle can shield an ally from damage.
Cast Evard's Black Tentacles without spending mana once per long rest, with temp HP and steady concentration.
Teleport yourself and up to five creatures to a body of water within a mile, once per short rest.

The Djinn Patron.about: Your patron is a genie of the elemental planes, bound to you by a bargain of wishes and words. Genie-pact warlocks make fine merchants and worse guests.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
A lamp, ring or bottle: retreat inside it for hours, and add extra elemental damage once per turn.
Resistance to your genie's damage type, and fly for 10 minutes a few times per long rest.
Bring up to five creatures into your vessel; a short rest there heals more.
Once per long-ish rest (1d4 long rests), cast any 6th-level or lower spell with a casting time of one action, without needing a tome. Your patron will remember the favor.

The Deathless.about: Your patron is a creature of death, and its gifts give you a grip on the grave. Deathless-pact warlocks are feared by the church and sought by the cults of the dead.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit your patron; your patron may teach them, as a debt.
Bonus action: transform for a minute, gaining temporary HP and immunity to fear, and your first hit each turn can frighten. Uses per long rest equal to proficiency bonus.
No need to eat, drink or breathe; once per turn, an attack can deal necrotic and extra damage in your dread form.
Resistance (immunity in dread form) to necrotic; once per long rest, burst back to 1 HP when you'd drop.
Project your spirit for an hour: fly, pass through objects and resist physical damage.

College of Courage.about: Bards who sing of battle and stand beside the people they celebrate. The College of Courage sends its members to the front lines with a song in their throat and a shield on their arm.
features: You train for the battlefield. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields and martial weapons.
Your Bardic Inspiration now lifts your allies in battle. An ally who has your Bardic Inspiration die can add it to a damage roll, or to its AC against one attack.
You can strike twice in one turn. Attack twice whenever you take the Attack action.
You weave spells into your strikes. When you cast a spell as an action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

College of Veils.about: Bards of fey enchantment, who sing of the wild courts and the beauty that hides their cruelty. Glamour bards are welcome at the balls of the great houses, and they leave every guest wanting more.
features: Your songs carry the glamour of the fey courts, and your listeners feel their pull. Spend Bardic Inspiration to give allies temporary HP and a free move without provoking.
Your performance can lift the spirits of those who hear it, and it can hold a few listeners spellbound. After performing for a minute, charm a few listeners for an hour (Wis save).
Your presence is so commanding that the whole court seems to bend toward you. For a minute, cast Command as a bonus action each turn without spending mana. Once per long rest.
Your majesty becomes a shield, and foes are compelled to turn toward you. Attackers must save (Cha) or choose a new target, once per short rest.

College of Blades.about: Bards who dance with a blade, combining swordplay with the rhythm of a song. Sword bards hold the stage in the taverns and the arenas.
features: You dance with a blade and wear your performance on your sleeve. Medium armor and the scimitar; use a weapon as your focus.
Your steel is sharp, and you know how to fight with a partner or alone. Dueling or Two-Weapon Fighting.

Your flourishes set your enemies off balance and turn each strike into a show. +10 ft speed when you attack, and spend Bardic Inspiration on a hit for a flourish: Guarding (add to AC), Cleaving (hit a second creature) or Nimble (push the target).
You strike twice whenever you take the Attack action. Attack twice when you take the Attack action.
You perform your flourishes with a flick of your blade, and the crowd roars. Use a d6 for a flourish instead of spending Bardic Inspiration.

College of Secrets.about: Bards who trade in secrets, rumours and quiet threats. Whisper bards are the spies of the bardic world, and they know which songs to sing to get a man to talk.
features: Your inspiration sharpens into psychic blades that bite through the mind as much as the flesh. Spend Bardic Inspiration on a hit for extra psychic damage (2d6, more at higher levels).
Your words can turn a face pale in the space of a conversation. Talk to someone alone for a minute and frighten them for an hour (Wis save).
You can take the shadow of a fallen foe and wear its face for a while. Capture the shadow of a humanoid who dies near you and wear its persona as a disguise.
A whisper in the right ear can bend a person to your will. Whisper to a creature to charm it into obeying you for 8 hours (Wis save), once per long rest.

College of Making.about: Bards who sing the world into being, and who believe a good song can change the shape of a room. Creation bards are often sought out by the craftsmen of the cities.
features: Your songs carry a spark of creation, and every inspiration holds a little potential. Your Bardic Inspiration carries a mote with an extra effect on checks, attacks or saves.
You shape objects out of song and performance, and they hold their form for a while. Create a nonmagical object worth up to 20 gp × bard level, once per long rest (or spend 10 mana to do it again).
Your performances can animate the objects you create into dancing companions. Animate a Large or smaller object as a dancing companion, once per long rest (or spend 18 mana).
Your creations flow out of you without limit, bounded only by your skill. Create several objects at once with Ballad of Making, with no gold limit.

College of Oratory.about: Bards who speak with perfect words and perfect timing, and who can talk a crowd out of anger or into a fight. Eloquent bards are rare, and the courts love them.
features: You speak with a grace that makes people listen and trust you. Persuasion and Deception rolls below 10 count as 10.
Your inspiration breaks a creature's concentration when it is most vulnerable. Spend Bardic Inspiration to subtract the roll from a creature's next save.
Your words linger in a listener's mind and keep working after you finish. A creature keeps your Bardic Inspiration die if the roll fails.
A few listeners understand your speech as though it were their own tongue. Make a few creatures understand you for an hour, once per long rest (or spend 5 mana).
Your inspiration spreads, and your allies carry it forward. When a creature succeeds with your inspiration, give another creature a free die.

College of Ghosts.about: Bards who call up the spirits of the dead through their song, and who listen to what the dead have to say. Spirit bards often find work in the cemeteries and the old battlefields.
features: You sing with the voices of the dead, and their wisdom comes to you as whispers. Learn Guidance, which reaches 60 ft.
Your focus is a token of the otherworld, and it carries your power. Use a candle, crystal ball, skull or tarot deck as your focus, and later add a d6 to spell damage or healing.
You can call a spirit's tale into your song, and its power will wait for you. Spend Bardic Inspiration to draw a spirit tale with a random effect you can use later.
A shared ritual brings the dead's knowledge to your companions. An hour-long ritual with allies to learn a divination or necromancy spell temporarily.
Your tales from beyond now come to you more reliably. Roll twice for Shade Tales and choose.

Circle of Lunar Forms.about: Druids who take on the forms of beasts under the light of the moon, and who fight as fiercely as any animal. Moon druids are respected by the hunters and feared by the herders.
features: Wild Shape as a bonus action, and while transformed spend mana to heal 1d8 per spell level of that mana (5 mana heals 1d8, 10 heals 2d8, 18 heals 3d8, and so on).
Turn into tougher beasts: up to CR 1 at 2nd, then CR equal to a third of your druid level from 6th.
Your beast attacks count as magical.
Spend two Wild Shape uses to become an air, earth, fire or water elemental.
Cast Alter Self at will, without spending mana.

Circle of Slumber.about: Druids who walk the dreams of the forest and speak to the fey in their sleep. Dream druids are welcome in the fey woods, and they sometimes forget to come back.
features: Your circle walks the dreams of the Summer Court, and you carry its healing into waking life. A pool of d6s (equal to druid level) to heal and give temporary HP with a bonus action.
You shelter your companions under a veil of moonlight and shadow during rest. During a rest, make a 30 ft sphere that hides and shelters your group.
You step between the paths of the fey woods as easily as crossing a room. Teleport 60 ft as a bonus action (or teleport a willing ally 30 ft), Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
You can slip into the dream-realm to scry, teleport or open a path to a distant place. After a short rest, cast Dream, Scrying or Teleportation Circle without spending mana, once per long rest.

Circle of the Herder.about: Druids who call on the spirits of the land and its beasts to guard their people. Shepherds keep the herds safe on the high pastures and the roads.
features: Speak with beasts and learn Sylvan.
Summon a spirit for a minute: Bear (temporary HP, advantage on Strength), Hawk (advantage on attacks with your reaction) or Unicorn (better healing and finding creatures). Once per short rest.
Beasts and fey you summon have extra HP and magical attacks.
Your summoned creatures heal at the end of their turns in your totem's aura.
When you drop to 0 HP, four beasts appear to protect you, once per long rest.

Circle of Mycelia.about: Druids who work with fungi and rot, turning death into a new kind of life. Spore druids are unwelcome in most villages, and they like it that way.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Reaction: deal necrotic damage to a creature that moves near you or starts its turn there (Con save).
Spend a Wild Shape use for temporary HP and stronger spores and melee necrotic damage.
Raise a beast or humanoid that dies near you as a zombie for an hour.
Throw your spore cloud into an area instead.
Immune to blinded, deafened, frightened and poisoned, and critical hits become normal hits.

Circle of the Heavens.about: Druids who read the constellations and draw their power from the night sky. Star druids are the astrologers of the wild, and they are often consulted before a voyage.
features: Learn Guidance, and cast Guiding Bolt without spending mana a few times per long rest.
Spend a Wild Shape use to become a constellation: Bowstar (radiant bolt), Cup of Light (heal extra when you heal), or Serpent (rolls below 10 on Int/Wis checks and concentration count as 10).
After a rest, gain weal or woe: add or subtract a d6 to others' rolls a few times.
Star Form gets stronger, and you can switch constellations each turn.
In Star Form, resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing.

Circle of Emberfire.about: Druids who work with flame and ash, and who believe fire renews the land. Wildfire druids are welcome in the burned country and avoided in the dry woods.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Spend a Wild Shape use to summon a fiery spirit that fights and can teleport you and allies.
Add a d8 to fire damage or healing spells while your spirit is out, and cast through it.
When a creature dies near your spirit, leave a flame you can use to heal or burn.
If you drop to 0 HP, your spirit sacrifices itself to bring you back to half HP.

Beast Warden.about: A ranger who fights alongside a loyal beast, and who knows the wild as well as any animal does. Beast Wardens are often found on the edge of the settled lands, where their companions are needed most.
features: You bond with a beast that fights beside you and obeys your commands. You may choose a primal beast of land, sea or sky instead, keeping the bond you form in the wild.
Your companion learns to fight as a partner. As a bonus action, it can Dash, Disengage or Help, and its attacks count as magical.
Your companion's wild strength takes over in a fight. It can attack twice whenever it takes the Attack action.
Your companion shares the magic you cast on yourself. Spells you cast on yourself also affect the companion while it is within range of you.

Shadow Hunter.about: A ranger who hunts in the dark and strikes from the shadows, and who is most at home in the night. Shadow Hunters are the watchers at the edge of the dark places.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Add Wisdom to initiative, and on your first turn move faster and make an extra attack with extra damage.
Darkvision, and creatures relying on darkvision can't see you in darkness.
Proficiency in Wisdom saves (or another save).
Once per turn, when you miss, make another attack.
Reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack against you.

Planewalker.about: A ranger who guards the borders between the planes and the lands they know well. Planewalkers see things that others do not, and they like it when others don’t ask about it.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Sense the nearest planar portal within a mile, once per short rest.
Bonus action: your next hit on a creature deals force damage and an extra 1d8 (2d8 at 11th).
Step into the Ethereal Plane for a turn, once per short rest.
Teleport 10 ft before each attack, and attack a third target if you hit two.
Reaction: gain resistance to an attack's damage.

Monster Bane.about: A ranger who hunts the dangerous creatures that prey on the living, and who has learned their weaknesses. Monster Bane are paid well by the villages and the great houses alike.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Learn a creature's immunities, resistances and vulnerabilities, Wisdom-mod times per long rest.
Mark a creature: your first hit on it each turn deals an extra 1d6.
Add a d6 to saves and grapple escapes against your prey.
Reaction: stop a creature casting a spell or teleporting (Wis save), once per short rest.
Reaction: when your prey forces a save, attack it; a hit makes you succeed.

Feywalker.about: A ranger who walks in the fey woods and carries a little of their magic. Feywalkers are welcome in the wild courts, and they are cautious about the bargains they make there.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Once per turn, a weapon hit deals an extra 1d4 psychic (1d6 at 11th).
Add Wisdom to Charisma checks, and gain one social skill.
Advantage against charm and fear, and redirect those effects at others.
Cast Summon Fey without spending mana once per long rest, without concentration if you choose a shorter duration.
Cast Misty Step without spending mana a few times, and take an ally with you.

Swarm Warden.about: A ranger who commands a swarm of tiny creatures, and who hears them whisper what they have seen. Swarm Wardens are easy to find in the marshes and hard to surprise anywhere.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Once per turn on a hit, your swarm deals 1d6 extra piercing, pushes the target, or moves you.
Fly slowly on your swarm for a minute, a few times per long rest.
Swarm damage grows to 1d8, and its push knocks prone or its move gives you half cover.
Reaction: gain resistance and teleport 30 ft as you scatter into the swarm.

Wyrmrider.about: A ranger who raises and rides a young dragon, and who has bonded with it for life. Wyrmriders are rare, and the lords of [[Dragonsneck]] would like to know how they do it.
features: Your bond with dragons teaches you their tongue and a few of their tricks. Learn Thaumaturgy and Draconic.
A young drake hatches for you and grows at your side. Summon a drake that fights beside you and grows with you.
As your drake grows, you ride it into the sky and share its hide. Your drake grows, can carry you while flying, and you gain resistance to its damage type.
Your drake can breathe a cone of its own element on your command. Breathe a cone of your drake's element (or command the drake to), once per long rest (or spend 18 mana).
Your drake reaches full size and fights with you like a true partner. The drake grows to Large, hits harder, and can shield you from damage.

Chaotic Origin.about: Your magic is unstable and surges out of you in strange ways. Wild mages are watched by the churches and the mage-guilds, who cannot agree on whether they are a blessing or a danger.
features: Your magic is wild and unpredictable, and it sometimes surges out of control. After casting a spell with mana, the DM can have you roll for a random wild magic effect.
Chaos leans toward you, and you can tip the scale of a roll in your favor. Gain advantage on one roll; regain it on a long rest or when the DM triggers a surge.
You can nudge a roll by a little, bending luck toward an ally or an enemy. Spend 2 sorcery points to add or subtract a d4 from someone else's roll.
Your surges become a weapon you can aim at will. Roll twice on the surge table and choose.
Your wild magic can strike harder when you roll the highest damage. When you roll maximum on a damage die, roll it again and add it, once per turn.

Heavenly Origin.about: Your magic comes from the gods, and you carry a spark of the divine in your blood. Heavenly-blooded casters are welcome in the temples, though not always in the councils.
features: A spark of the divine burns in your blood, and it lends you knowledge of the gods' own spells. Learn spells from the cleric list as well as the sorcerer list, and gain one affinity spell (good, evil, law, chaos or neutrality).
Fortune smiles on you when you need it most. Add 2d4 to a failed save or missed attack, once per short rest.
Your magic can knit wounds and turn healing into a cascade of renewed strength. Spend 1 sorcery point to reroll healing dice.
Spectral wings unfurl from your back, and the sky opens to you. Sprout spectral wings and fly.
Even as you fall, the gods' favor pulls you back from the brink. Regain half your HP as a bonus action when below half, once per long rest.

Umbral Origin.about: Your magic draws on the darkness and the things that live in it. Shadow sorcerers are feared in the cities and useful in the places the watch cannot reach.
features: Darkvision 120 ft, and cast Darkness with 2 sorcery points (you can see through it).
When you'd drop to 0 HP, Cha save to stay at 1 HP, once per long rest.
Spend 3 sorcery points to summon a shadow hound that hunts a target and makes it worse at saving against your spells.
In dim light or darkness, teleport 120 ft as a bonus action.
Spend 6 sorcery points to become shadowy for a minute: resist most damage and move through objects.

Tempest Origin.about: Your magic is the storm itself, and the wind and waves answer your call. Storm sorcerers are sought out by sailors and avoided by the captains who want their ships to stay afloat.
features: You learn the speech of the storm and the wind that carries it. Speak Primordial and its dialects.
Your magic lifts you on the wind and lets you float a little while the storm rages. Fly 10 ft without provoking after casting a spell with mana.
Lightning and thunder cannot easily harm you, and they strengthen your spells. Resistance to lightning and thunder, and a burst of storm damage when you cast those spells.
You command the rain and wind near you, and they answer your call. Control rain and wind around you.
When a foe strikes you in melee, a surge of lightning answers. Reaction: lightning damage and a push against a creature that hits you in melee.
In time, you become a creature of the wind, able to fly and share the sky with others. Immune to lightning and thunder, fly 60 ft, and share flight with allies for an hour.

Aberrant Origin.about: Your magic comes from an alien mind that has touched your own, and its thoughts leak into yours. Aberrant sorcerers are unsettling company, and the scholars want to study them.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Link minds with a creature to talk telepathically.
Cast your psionic spells with sorcery points instead of mana, with no components.
Resistance to psychic, advantage against charm and fear.
Spend sorcery points for strange gifts: see invisible, fly, swim and breathe water, or squeeze through tiny gaps.
Teleport and pull creatures where you left with force damage, once per long rest (or 5 sorcery points).

Clockwork Origin.about: Your magic comes from the order of the cosmos, and you feel the gears of the world turning. Clockwork sorcerers keep the balance of the isles, and they dislike disorder of any kind.
features: Avarenth: subclasses add no spells. These suit the path; learn them from tomes or teachers at the usual cost.
Reaction: cancel advantage or disadvantage on a roll nearby, Proficiency-bonus times per long rest.
Spend sorcery points to give a creature a ward of d8s that soaks damage.
For a minute, attacks against you can't have advantage and your rolls below 10 count as 10, once per long rest.
Summon spirits of order to heal, repair and end spells, once per long rest.

School of Warding.about: Wizards who learn to protect, banish and shield, and who build wards that keep the dangerous out. Abjurers are the first hired to guard the great houses.
features: You study the arts of warding and protection, and you learn to shield the innocent. Copying abjuration spells costs half the gold and time.
You weave a ward around yourself that soaks up harm as you cast. When you cast an abjuration spell with mana, you make a ward that absorbs damage, recharged by more abjuration spells.
Your ward can guard an ally who stands near you. Use your ward to absorb damage for an ally nearby.
Your knowledge of wards makes you sharper at the abjuration arts. Add your proficiency bonus to ability checks made with abjuration spells (like Counterspell and Dispel Magic).
You become resistant to magic, and spells lose their hold on you. Advantage on saves against spells and resistance to spell damage.

School of Summoning.about: Wizards who summon and transport things across the world, and who can bring a friend or a foe to their side in a heartbeat. Conjurers are the couriers of the mage-guilds.
features: Your spellbook holds the knowledge of summoning and of the quick step between places. Copying conjuration spells costs half the gold and time.
You can pull a small, ordinary object out of thin air to use for a while. Conjure a small nonmagical object for an hour.
You slip across short distances, trading places with a friend when a fight turns bad. Teleport 30 ft, or swap places with an ally, once per long rest (or after casting a conjuration spell).
Your summons hold steady even when you are struck while calling them. Damage can't break your concentration on conjuration spells.
The creatures you call arrive with a bit of extra strength to hold the line. Creatures you summon get 30 temporary HP.

School of Foresight.about: Wizards who see the future and the hidden truth, and who read the signs that others miss. Diviners are consulted by lords before they make a choice.
features: Copying divination spells costs half the gold and time.
After a long rest, roll two d20s and keep them; replace any roll you see with one (three dice at 14th).
When you cast a divination spell of 2nd level or higher with mana, regain the mana cost of a spell one level lower (up to 40, a 5th-level spell).
Gain darkvision, ethereal sight, the ability to read any language, or see invisible things until your next rest.

School of Charm.about: Wizards who bend minds and charm people, and who can make a crowd agree with them. Enchanters are welcome at court and watched closely by the church.
features: You study the mind's soft places and learn how to bend a will with a few words. Copying enchantment spells costs half the gold and time.
A gentle word and a steady gaze can soften a stranger into a willing listener. Charm a creature next to you and leave it dazed while you hold its gaze.
Your charm slips into a creature's thoughts and turns them away from their target. Reaction: force an attacker to target someone else (Wis save).
Your enchantments can bind a second creature alongside the first. Single-target enchantment spells can target a second creature.
You can rewrite a creature's recent memories so the charm leaves no trace. Make a creature you charmed forget it was charmed and lose some hours of memory.

School of Phantasms.about: Wizards who make the world look like something it is not, and who can hide an army in a single room. Illusionists are the best liars in the isles.
features: You have a gift for copying illusion spells. Copying an illusion spell into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.
Your Minor Illusion now makes both a sound and an image, so one cantrip can fool more than one sense.
You can reshape an illusion you are maintaining. As an action, change the appearance of an illusion you have created and are concentrating on.
Reaction: when a creature attacks you, an illusory double appears and makes the attack miss. You can use this once per short rest.
You can make a piece of your illusion real. Choose one non-living object within your illusion; it becomes real for one minute.

School of Death.about: Wizards who study death and bring the dead back for a time. Necromancers are hunted by the church and sought by the desperate.
features: You copy necromancy spells with ease. Copying a necromancy spell into your spellbook costs half the usual gold and time.
You feed on the death you cause. When you kill a creature with a spell, regain hit points equal to twice the spell's level, or three times if the spell is a necromancy spell of 1st level or higher.
Your dead serve you better. Animate Dead raises one extra creature, and each undead you create gains bonus hit points equal to your wizard level.
Death no longer frightens you. You gain resistance to necrotic damage, and your hit point maximum can't be reduced.
You take command of the dead. As an action, choose an undead creature you can see within 60 ft; it must make a Charisma save or become your ally until you lose control of it.

School of Alchemy.about: Wizards who change one thing into another, and who believe any substance can be reshaped with the right words. Transmuters are the alchemists of the mage-guilds.
features: You learn to change matter into new forms, and you believe any substance can be reshaped. Copying transmutation spells costs half the gold and time.
You alter the nature of common materials for a short while. Change one material into another (wood, stone, iron, copper or silver) for an hour.
You shape a magic stone that holds a transmutation of your choosing. Make a stone that gives darkvision, speed, a save proficiency or a resistance.
You can reshape your own body with a spell cast at will. Cast Polymorph on yourself without spending mana, once per short rest.
You unlock the stone's full power to reshape the world around you. Destroy your stone for a big effect: transform an object, cure everything, cast Raise Dead, or restore youth.

Spellsword.about: Mages who didn't trade the sword for the book. A Spellsword wizard wears plate, swings steel and still reaches for the high spells, but the armor takes its toll on the weave.
features: You gain proficiency with Medium armor, Heavy armor, Shields and Martial weapons.
A weapon you are proficient with works as your Spellcasting Focus, and you can perform the Somatic components of spells even when you have weapons or a Shield in one or both hands.
While you wear Heavy armor, spells of level 3 or higher cost 5 extra mana to cast.
After you cast a spell of level 1 or higher, your next weapon hit before the end of your next turn deals extra Force damage equal to twice the spell's level.
When a creature hits you with an attack, you can spend 5 mana and use your Reaction to add your Intelligence modifier to your Armor Class against that attack.
You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Weight of Plate no longer applies to you, and you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration while you wear armor.

Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you enter a fusion of steel and spell for 1 minute. For the duration, you can make one weapon attack as a Bonus Action after you cast any spell on your turn, and your weapon hits ignore Resistance.

School of Battle Magic.about: Wizards who fight in the front lines and cast their spells with the blade. War mages serve the armies of the great houses, and they are the first to be wounded.
features: Reaction: when a creature you can see hits you or a creature within 10 ft, gain +2 AC or +4 to a save. You can only cast cantrips on your next turn.
You read the field the moment a fight starts. Add your Intelligence modifier to your initiative.
When you counter or dispel a spell, you store a surge of raw force. Spend stored surges to add extra force damage to your spells, and the surges fade at the end of a long rest.
Your concentration is hardened by years of fighting while casting. You gain +2 AC and +2 to saving throws while you concentrate on a spell.
Arcane Parry now also bursts outward. Creatures within 10 ft of you take force damage when you use it, so your deflection becomes a counterattack.

Timecraft.about: Wizards who bend time for a moment, and who see the past and the future in a single breath. Timecrafters are rare and cautious, and the wise do not ask them to rush.
features: You bend time to suit your will, and the past and future are your playground. Reaction: force a creature to reroll an attack, check or save, twice per long rest.
You sense the flow of time around you and react faster than others. Add Intelligence to initiative.
You can freeze a foe in the flow of time for a moment. Freeze a Large or smaller creature in time (Con save), a few times per long rest.
You can store a spell in a bead for another to use later. Store a 4th-level or lower spell in a bead someone else can use, once per short rest.
You can see the future before it happens and choose which path to take. Decide whether a roll you can see succeeds or fails, at the cost of a level of exhaustion.

Weightcraft.about: Wizards who shape gravity itself, dragging foes to the ground and lifting the heavy as if they were light. Weightcrafters are feared for their power and respected for their care.
features: You bend the weight of a creature. As an action, make a creature heavier or lighter for one minute, changing how far it can move and how hard it hits the ground.
Your spells pull their targets along with them. When a spell you cast hits or affects a creature, you can move that creature up to 5 ft.
You can turn gravity into force. Reaction: add extra damage to an attack, or to falling damage, a few times per long rest.
You create a field that drags enemies toward you and holds them in place. Once per long rest, or by spending 18 mana, a creature in the field must move toward you and cannot move on its turn.

Order of the Inkwright.about: Wizards who write the spells they learn into their own books, and who can copy a spell from any page. Inkwrights are the librarians of the mage-guilds and the keepers of its secrets.
features: Your spellbook is more than a book; it is a magical quill and an ink that writes itself. A magical quill that copies spells quickly and cheaply.
Your spellbook awakens, and its pages answer your call. Swap a spell's damage type for another from your book, and cast rituals faster.
Your spellbook takes a shape of its own and can cast spells from where it rests. Make your book's spirit appear and cast spells from its location.
You write scrolls of spells you know, and your hand strengthens each one you make. Make a magic scroll of a spell you know after a long rest, cast as one level higher.
You fuse yourself to your book's words, and you can turn its power to your defense. Advantage on Arcana checks, and let your book take damage for you by erasing spells temporarily.

_note: Short summaries written for Avarenth in our own words, not the book text. Check the exact wording in your copy of the book. Spell-slot costs are given in mana.

Automaton-Wright.about: Builders of clockwork companions. An Automaton-Wright's first masterwork is a brass automaton that fights at their side, and most of them talk to it more than to people. Guild halls in [[Stonehelm]] keep rows of retired automatons standing in honor.
features: You gain proficiency with smith's tools. If you already have it, pick another artisan's tool.

You build a Medium brass automaton. It acts on your turn and does what you command with a bonus action; otherwise it defends itself and you. It has AC 15, hit points equal to 2 + your Intelligence modifier + five times your Cogwright level, and a slam that deals 1d8 + your proficiency bonus force damage. As a reaction it can raise an arm to give an attacker within 5 feet disadvantage. You can repair it with tinker's tools during a rest, or rebuild it after a long rest if it is destroyed.
When you attack with a weapon fitted with one of your Tinkerings, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity.
You can attack twice when you take the Attack action.

When you or your automaton hits a creature, you can push the gears past their limit: deal an extra 2d6 force damage, or instead let a creature within 30 feet of the automaton regain 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier hit points. You can do this a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier per long rest.
Overclock now deals or heals 4d6. Your automaton's defending arm also strikes back, dealing 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier force damage to the attacker.

Ironclad.about: Cogwrights who build themselves a second body of plate and pistons. Ironclads stand at the front of dwarven shield walls, and every suit is fitted to its wearer over years of work.
features: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

You can turn a suit of armor you wear into a clockwork engine. It covers your whole body, ignores any Strength requirement, can't be removed against your will, and lets you use your Intelligence modifier for attacks with its built-in weapons. Choose a pattern after a long rest: Bulwark, with thunder gauntlets (1d8 thunder) that give a struck creature disadvantage against anyone but you, and a defensive spring that grants temporary hit points; or Shade, with a lightning bolt-caster (1d6 lightning, 90 feet) that adds 1d6 once per turn, quieter joints, and advantage on Stealth checks.
You can attack twice when you take the Attack action.
Your Clockwork Plate can hold more upgrades. It counts as up to four separate items for your Tinkerings, and those Tinkerings don't count against your limit.

Bulwark: as a reaction, a creature you can see within 30 feet that fails a Strength save is dragged up to 25 feet toward you, and you can strike it if it ends next to you. Shade: a creature hit by your bolt-caster glows until your next turn, and the next attack against it has advantage and deals an extra 1d6 lightning.

Siege-Wright.about: Engineers of turrets, bolt throwers and things that explode on purpose. Siege-Wrights man the walls of every dwarven hold, and the Guild keeps a careful list of who has blown up what.
features: As an action you set down a small clockwork turret within 5 feet. Choose its mechanism: Bolt Thrower (ranged attack, 2d8 force, 120 feet), Flame Jet (a 15-foot cone, Dexterity save, 2d8 fire), or Shield Spring (a creature within 10 feet gains 1d8 + your Intelligence modifier temporary hit points). Trigger it with a bonus action. It lasts an hour. You can set one for free once per long rest; another costs 5 mana.
You make a rod or wand of brass and crystal. While you cast through it, add 1d8 to one damage roll of your spells each turn.

As an action, you can detonate your turret: each creature within 20 feet of it makes a Dexterity save, taking 3d10 force damage on a failure or half on a success. Your turrets' damage and healing rise by 1d8.
You can keep two turrets running at once and trigger both with one bonus action. Allies within 10 feet of a turret have half cover.

Tonic-Wright.about: Steam alchemists who brew tonics in brass stills and pressure vials. Tonic-Wrights are the Guild's healers and its quiet poisoners, and a few of the oldest stills in [[Stonehelm]] have been running for a hundred years.
features: After a long rest you brew one steam tonic in a sealed vial, and more at higher levels. You can brew another by spending mana. A creature that drinks or breathes a tonic gets one effect: Mending (regain 2d4 + your Intelligence modifier hit points), Quickening (+10 feet of speed for an hour), Hardening (+1 AC for 10 minutes), Clearing (see in darkness to 60 feet for an hour), or Lightening (fall slowly and jump twice as far for 10 minutes).
When you cast a spell through your alchemist's tools, add your Intelligence modifier to one roll of its acid, fire or poison damage, or to the hit points it restores.

Your tonics also grant 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier temporary hit points. You can cast Lesser Restoration a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier per long rest without spending mana.
You resist acid and poison damage and can't be poisoned. Once per long rest you can cast Greater Restoration or Heal without spending mana or using components.
